Welcome! I’m glad you’re here, because we’re about to take a fascinating journey together. Have you ever wondered how the financial world grew so powerful, or why so many businesses seem to care more about quick profits than real innovation? In Makers and Takers: The Rise of Finance and the Fall of American Business, Rana Foroohar invites us behind the scenes—showing how Wall Street’s priorities have started to overshadow the creativity and hard work that once powered Main Street. Instead of building great products or investing in people, more and more companies chase after stock prices and short-term gains. That shift doesn’t just change balance sheets—it changes lives, affecting workers, families, and entire communities.
As we dig in, we’ll uncover the forces that put finance in the driver’s seat, and explore how corporate decisions now revolve around buybacks and clever financial maneuvers—while real investment takes a back seat. Through powerful stories and sharp insights, Rana Foroohar paints a picture of an economy where the balance between making and taking has tipped, and invites us to imagine what it might take to bring back fairness, innovation, and true growth.
So, join me as we unravel the story behind America’s changing business landscape—because understanding these shifts isn’t just interesting, it’s essential for all of us.
